title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale
abstract: arXiv:2611.07088v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Symbolic models offer a powerful account of cognition, but their scope has historically been limited by the need for hand-engineering and computational tractability. We show how advances in artificial intelligence (AI) can scale symbolic modeling and help overcome these engineering limitations. We introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS)---an approach for automated search of interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs that verifiably reproduce behavior---and apply it to model both human and machine behavior across hundreds of challenging reasoning problems. Analyzing these programs reveals that both people and machines tend to oversimplify, adopt rules that are partial explanations for their observations, and misinfer dependencies between problem features. These shared signatures are modulated by available resources, with reasoning effort predicting the extent to which machines simplify and explain their observations.

translated_title: 大规模合成人类与机器推理的符号模型
translated_abstract: 符号模型为认知提供了强有力的解释框架，但其应用范围历来受到手工工程需求和计算可处理性的限制。我们展示了人工智能（AI）的进步如何能够扩展符号建模并帮助克服这些工程局限。我们提出了行为条件化符号合成——一种自动搜索可解释、确定性符号程序的方法，这些程序能够可验证地复现行为——并将其应用于对人类和机器在数百个具有挑战性的推理问题上的行为进行建模。通过分析这些程序，我们发现人类和机器都倾向于过度简化，采用仅能部分解释其观察结果的规则，并错误推断问题特征之间的依赖关系。这些共同的行为特征受可用资源的调节，推理努力程度可以预测机器简化和解释其观察结果的程度。
tldr: 提出行为条件化符号合成（BCSS）方法，利用AI自动搜索可解释的确定性符号程序，大规模建模人类与机器的推理行为，并揭示两者在推理中都存在过度简化和错误推断问题特征依赖关系的共同特征。
en_tdlr: We introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS), an AI-driven approach that automatically discovers interpretable symbolic programs to model human and machine reasoning at scale, revealing that both tend to oversimplify and misinfer dependencies between problem features.
